content: Brzycki formula: 1RM = load * 36 / (37 - reps). Best agreement with measured 1RM in the 2-10 rep range; error grows above 10 reps as muscular endurance (not maximal strength) starts dominating the limiting factor, and the formula is mathematically undefined/blows up as reps approaches 37 (denominator -> 0). Epley (load*(1+reps/30)) has no hard breakdown point but is documented to over-estimate at high reps for the same physiological reason. Neither pure formula is reliable above ~15-20 reps -- an empirical %1RM-by-reps lookup table (e.g. NSCA/Baechle table, capped/interpolated, with a floor for very high rep counts) is the safer approach for bodyweight work that regularly goes into the 15-30 rep range, matching D-18's 'rep-max table / Brzycki hybrid' instruction.
